name: More Cowbell
description: Kevin Sun wants to move his precious collection of n cowbells from Naperthrill to Exeter, where there is actually grass instead of corn. Before moving, he must pack his cowbells into k boxes of a fixed size. In order to keep his collection safe during transportation, he won't place more than two cowbells into a single box. Since Kevin wishes to minimize expenses, he is curious about the smallest size box he can use to pack his entire collection. Kevin is a meticulous cowbell collector and knows that the size of his i -th ( 1 ≤ i ≤ n ) cowbell is an integer s i . In fact, he keeps his cowbells sorted by size, so s i - 1 ≤ s i for any i > 1 . Also an expert packer, Kevin can fit one or two cowbells into a box of size s if and only if the sum of their sizes does not exceed s . Given this information, help Kevin determine the smallest s for which it is possible to put all of his cowbells into k boxes of size s .
input_specification: The first line of the input contains two space-separated integers n and k ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 2· k ≤ 100 000 ), denoting the number of cowbells and the number of boxes, respectively. The next line contains n space-separated integers s 1 , s 2 , ..., s n ( 1 ≤ s 1 ≤ s 2 ≤ ... ≤ s n ≤ 1 000 000 ), the sizes of Kevin's cowbells. It is guaranteed that the sizes s i are given in non-decreasing order.
output_specification: Print a single integer, the smallest s for which it is possible for Kevin to put all of his cowbells into k boxes of size s .
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 604B — More Cowbell [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
